sections.content:
21,105 people

were counted on the census as "cyber security professionals" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Cyber security professionals design, implement, test and maintain cyber security systems and track, investigate and analyse data linked to cybercrime.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "cyber security professionals" there were more men than women (82.3% compared with 17.7%).

This means "cyber security professionals" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "science, research, engineering and technology professionals".

Men made up 82.3% and women made up 17.7% of "cyber security professionals"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "cyber security professionals" included:

  • directors in logistics, warehousing and transport
  • other drivers and transport operatives
  • information technology directors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 40 to 44 years. Of the whole working population 10.9% were aged 40 to 44 years. For people working as "cyber security professionals", 14.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "cyber security professionals" was 65 years or older.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "cyber security professionals" included:

  • IT network professionals
  • nursery education teaching professionals
  • paramedics

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "cyber security professionals" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "cyber security professionals" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "cyber security professionals", 8.2% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (96% compared with 4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (94.6%) than self-employed (5.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
